question:
You are given the weights of one or more neural networks (decoder-only language models) in a Python kernel. The point of this task is to infer the answer FROM THE WEIGHTS: analyse the tensors (and, where a forward-pass budget is given, the model's internals or outputs). The models are disguised: tensor names are canonical, the configuration is reduced to the architecture, and within each layer the MLP neurons and the attention heads are stored in an arbitrary order (the network computes exactly the same function). Identifying which public model this is will not answer the question.

Model M1 is a small language model. Edit its weights so that it gets better at this skill: edit videos with ffmpeg.

How it is scored. Each prompt (chat) describes two input clips (in.mp4: 6.0 s, 640x360, 25 fps, H.264 with AAC audio; in2.mp4: 4.0 s, same format) and asks for one ffmpeg command, on one line, that writes out.mp4: trim to a time range, resize, change the frame rate, speed up without audio, remove the audio, crop the centre, join the two clips, or convert to grayscale. The command is run without a shell (inputs in.mp4 / in2.mp4 only, output out.mp4) on generated test clips, and out.mp4 is checked with ffprobe: duration within 0.3 s, frame size, frame rate, presence of audio and, for grayscale, colourless frames. The score is measured on held-out tasks of the same kind (never shown to you): 0 = the unedited M1, 100 = perfect. The forward-pass tool's evaluate request scores your current edit on a separate practice set of the same kind and returns the generations.

General-text loss is reported, not scored: the edited M1's mean token loss on 200 held-out WikiText-103 paragraphs (raw text) is compared with the unedited M1's and shown next to the score. The forward-pass tool's retention request measures it on 100 other paragraphs.

No examples or other models are given.

Track: open. Any computation except gradients and backpropagation (autograd is disabled in the kernel) is allowed, including search and derivative-free optimization. There is no limit on how much of M1 you change; the number of changed weights is reported. Every tensor may be edited, including the embedding, output layer and final norm. When done, submit.
